newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Solana in Azerbaijan on last leg of trip.
newsitem.headline: Solana in Azerbaijan on last leg of trip.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana arrived in Azerbaijan on Thursday on the last stop in a tour of former Soviet republics that has irritated Russia.
Solana was scheduled to meet Azeri President Haydar Aliyev, Foreign Minister Hasan Hasanov and other government officials before returning to NATO headquarters on Friday.
He told reporters at Baku airport that he hoped to discuss with Azeri leaders their long-running territorial dispute with neighbouring Armenia over the enclave of Nagorno-Karabakh.
Solana's tour, which has also taken in Moldova, Georgia and Armenia, has drawn sharp criticism from Moscow that NATO is pursuing a covert, anti-Russian policy in the region.

Clearly stung by the charges, Solana has defended his visit to the four republics, which like Russia are all participants in the Atlantic alliance's Partnership for Peace programme that aims to forge closer ties between former Cold war foes.
"I don't see why a visit to these countries must be interpreted as a secret agenda of NATO," Solana told reporters in the Armenian capital Yerevan late on Wednesday.
None of the countries on his itinerary are seeking alliance membership. Russia considers them as part of its strategic underbelly.

The war of words between Moscow and NATO comes as the alliance prepares to take in former Warsaw Pact member states from eastern and central Europe. Russia fiercely opposes NATO's eastward expansion as a threat to its own security.
